verdicts.correction: Not every pinned pnpm 11+ project gets the env document. Per pnpm's lockfile docs, packageManagerDependencies (first YAML document) is written when the project declares devEngines.packageManager, or pins pnpm 12 or newer through the legacy packageManager field; configDependencies also go there. pnpm init writes devEngines.packageManager since v11, so new projects hit it by default. A pnpm 11 pin through the legacy packageManager field does not write it. pmOnFail: ignore removes the document only because pnpm then stops enforcing the pinned version.

recommendation_issues.problem: pmOnFail: ignore is not free. pnpm's lockfile page says 'pnpm then doesn't enforce the pinned version, so it has nothing to record', so the plan's 'sürümü depoda sabit' then holds only where something installs that exact version (pnpm/setup in CI, the Docker image tag, eas.json); the developer machine runs whatever pnpm is installed. The Turkish text must say this. The proposed fallback to pnpm 10 is the weakest exit: pnpm/setup installs only v11+, minimumReleaseAge defaults to 0 before v11, trustLockfile starts at 11.3.0. A fallback that keeps pnpm's own enforcement and a single-document lockfile is pnpm 11 pinned through the legacy packageManager field with no devEngines.packageManager (https://pnpm.io/lockfile); its cost is that pnpm deploy dropped the injectWorkspacePackages requirement only in v12.2.0 (https://pnpm.io/cli/deploy).

'ayrıca yazmam' keeps pnpm in loose mode, where per the 11.1.3 release notes pnpm 'auto-adds the immature picks to minimumReleaseAgeExclude in pnpm-workspace.yaml and lets the install proceed'. The 1-day hold becomes a preference and the exclude list grows by itself. The reason given for not writing the value (dependabot-core #16375) was fixed by PR #16376, merged 2026-10-01. The sentence should either set minimumReleaseAge explicitly (strict) or keep the default and say new minimumReleaseAgeExclude lines are reviewed in each diff.

'Sürüm tek dosyada (.node-version) yazılır; Docker imajı ve EAS derlemesi aynı sürümü kullanır' overstates it. EAS reads Node from the eas.json 'node' field (https://docs.expo.dev/eas/json/) and the Dockerfile carries its own base tag, so the version lives in three places that must match. Also Node 26 is still 'Current' until its LTS date in schedule.json, so the plan's own 'LTS dışı sürüm kullanılmaz' needs the wording 'Node 26 (LTS)' rather than an unqualified start.

pnpm/setup is young: v1.0.0 'Ready for production use' on 15 June 2026, v3.0.0 on 2026-09-20, 144 stars, three majors in about three months (https://github.com/pnpm/setup/releases). Acceptable because pnpm/action-setup's README recommends it for pnpm 11+, but it raises the value of S01-11's full-SHA pin; expect more majors.

As written the replacement is weaker than the check it removes. The project domain is opt-in ('project': 'recommended' or the rule set explicitly, https://biomejs.dev/linter/domains/); the rule's default severity is warning, so biome ci passes unless it is set to error; exports without a tag are public, so a forgotten @package tag silently allows a cross-module import. test/support data builders and any file that gathers all Drizzle tables would need an override. Accept only if the plan names: rule as error, @package on every module-internal export (or a non-public default visibility, which the rule page says is configurable), and a test override. Otherwise keep dependency-cruiser until the TS 7 move; it is maintained (18.5.0 on 2026-09-30, two maintainers) and blocks nothing that openapi-typescript does not already block.
Inconsistent with S01-09: S01-05 names dependency-cruiser as a TS 7 blocker while S01-09 removes it. Whichever is accepted, the final plan text must list the same tools.

Minor: the changed-only filter compares against the merge base since pnpm 12.7.0 and needs Git 2.24+ and the base branch history in the CI checkout (https://pnpm.io/filtering). For three apps and two packages, plain pnpm -r for every run is simpler; the filter should be an option, not the default.

Removing @fastify/cors is safe in production only. In development the panel runs on Vite's own dev server port, so calls to the API are cross-origin unless Vite's server.proxy forwards /v1 ('Configure custom proxy rules for the dev server', https://vite.dev/config/server-options). The recommendation must name the Vite proxy or the dev panel breaks. Caddy's automatic HTTPS also needs the domain's A/AAAA records on the server and ports 80 and 443 open externally (https://caddyserver.com/docs/automatic-https), which a university network may refuse; then the institution's proxy and certificate are the path.

react must not share one catalog entry between panel and mobile. Expo SDK 57 fixes React at 19.2.3 (https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/) while npm latest is 19.3.0, and Expo CLI docs say React Native packages 'often need to be the exact right version'. A shared entry makes every panel React bump a mobile bump, and a Dependabot catalog PR would move the app off the SDK set. Keep expo, expo-*, react and react-native out of the shared catalog; typescript, zod and vitest are fine there.

Names two tunnel products for one job. Pick one in the plan: Cloudflare Quick Tunnel needs no account but its hostname changes on every run, which forces a new API URL into each test build; if that matters, Tailscale alone.

Minor: pnpm already has the route for urgent fixes. pnpm audit --fix writes the minimum patched version into minimumReleaseAgeExclude (pnpm 11.0 release notes), which is shorter than a manual edit; the 'oturunca çıkarırım' clause still applies.

misses.finding: The plan never says how server TypeScript runs in development, in the Cucumber and Vitest runs, and inside the image (line 714: 'Sunucu imajı çok aşamalı derlenir'). Node's type stripping is stable since v24.12.0 and v25.2.0, so Node 26 runs .ts files directly with no tsx or ts-node. Limits: no enum, namespace with runtime code or parameter properties, tsconfig paths are not applied, no type checking, and Node refuses .ts files under node_modules, which is where pnpm deploy places packages/core and packages/contracts, so those two must ship as JS in the image. The flags Node recommends (erasableSyntaxOnly, verbatimModuleSyntax) also suit the TS 7 path. Cucumber's own docs still suggest tsx for TypeScript steps, so that one runner may keep it.

verdict_reason: All 18 findings re-checked against their cited sources plus at least one independent primary source (npm registry, vendor docs, release notes). 17 CONFIRMED, 1 CORRECTED (S01-01, high: the trigger for pnpm's env lockfile document is narrower than stated, the Dependabot alert risk itself is confirmed), 0 REFUTED, 0 UNVERIFIABLE. 33 checked_ok items with versions, dates or setting names spot-checked against the registry and docs; none disputed. 7 misses, none high (2 medium: Expo-managed packages under Dependabot, TypeScript execution path on Node 26; 5 low). 11 recommendation issues, the heaviest being S01-01 (pmOnFail: ignore drops pnpm's own version enforcement), S01-09 (Biome rule opt-in and warning-level as written) and S01-18 (react in a shared catalog fights Expo's pins); these need wording fixes before the plan absorbs them. The net moving-part count of the accepted recommendations stays negative.
